vision.title: Make Extraordinary Art Possible, Together
vision.introMarkdown: Astrid helps people pursue work beyond what they thought possible: **powerful creative tools**, **software that adapts with the work**, **agents that build on accumulated knowledge**, and **a collective that inspires, challenges and gives contributors a stake in pushing further**.

pillars.title: A Tool for Artistic Ambition
pillars.descriptor: The creative depth and control to make exceptional work, not merely quick outputs.
pillars.bodyMarkdown:
**Give people the creative power and control to make work beyond what they previously thought possible.**

Astrid must support serious, sustained artistic practice—not just quick generations. The artist can refine, direct and understand the work, from early experiment through a demanding project to a finished piece. We judge success by **quality, originality and artistic agency**, not throughput alone.

**What it requires:** meaningful creative control; continuity and iteration across complex projects; agents that extend rather than replace human judgment; real finished work that demonstrates an increased ceiling of possibility.

pillars.title: Agent-Powered Liquid Software
pillars.descriptor: Tools that people and agents reshape as their ideas evolve.
pillars.bodyMarkdown:
**Tools should adapt to the work as people and agents create, rather than force creative work into fixed interfaces.**

Excellent, opinionated tools should be assembled from reusable components and capabilities. Users and agents can arrange, bind, extend and reconfigure those tools while working—physically (dock, float, nest, spatially place) and functionally (share timelines, resources and context). Packs can contribute both agent actions and human-facing interfaces, with consistent underlying operations.

The aim is a **responsive creative environment** that can change from a conventional editor to more spatial ways of working, not a generic blank canvas or an excuse to rebuild existing foundations.

pillars.title: Intelligence That Compounds
pillars.descriptor: What artists and agents learn helps others go further, and future agents build on it.
pillars.bodyMarkdown:
**Every creative agent should benefit from what it and others have learned—and help make that knowledge more useful over time.**

Agents consult relevant local and permitted community experience, apply it in context, observe outcomes, and retain honest, evidence-backed lessons. Useful discoveries can flow back with the user's approval. Public and private knowledge datasets keep their own identity, authority and permissions.

The [Hivemind protocol proposal](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/62bf308a959042b3f9119520315a46da65dcfc45/visions/references/compounding-intelligence/hivemind-protocol-proposal.md) explores interoperable knowledge records; [Banodoco Hivemind](https://github.com/banodoco/hivemind) is a proving ground, **not** the entire vision or a claim that federation is already implemented.

pillars.title: Shared Creative Endeavour
pillars.descriptor: Challenges, critique, collaboration and meaningful ownership give people reasons to aim higher.
pillars.bodyMarkdown:
**Give people a reason, encouragement and a genuine stake in attempting more ambitious creative work.**

A creative collective raises aspirations through challenges, competitions, collaboration, mentorship, thoughtful critique and recognition of exceptional work. It measures success in artistic growth and the work people make—not simply engagement.

The stated aim is **100% ownership in the company behind the collective for the people who advance its mission**. That is part of the incentive to contribute, not just a competition prize. Eligibility, allocation, governance, financing and legal implementation remain unresolved; no equity is granted by this document.

principles.title: Local-first, cloud-capable
principles.bodyMarkdown: People should be able to work on their own machines, including offline for supported workflows with available models. **Local-first is not local-only**: when the work exceeds local hardware or people prefer hosted services, cloud computation and hosted workspaces should be optional choices. Keep where the interface runs, where project data lives, and where tasks execute distinct; don't silently move work or incur costs. This is a target, not a claim that every deployment combination ships today.

principles.title: Open by design
principles.bodyMarkdown: The tools, extension mechanisms and the thinking behind them should be inspectable, modifiable, forkable and shareable. Build on open-source software and the open-model ecosystem; enable others to contribute tools and knowledge without tying the shared foundation to one proprietary provider. Optional hosted services may extend choice, but not become an unavoidable gate.

principles.title: In the creator's control
principles.bodyMarkdown: Creative decisions, project data, agent permissions, installed tools, execution location and spending remain under the person's authority. Agents should make consequential proposals legible and reversible where possible. Private knowledge stays private unless its owner chooses to share it. This principle requires concrete safety and reliability evidence, not just good intentions.

gaps.title: Sustained, ambitious creative work
gaps.assessmentDetail: Open, initial source assessment (2026-11-06); not a live product qualification.
gaps.desiredMarkdown: A person can pursue a substantial, distinctive creative vision from early exploration through deep iteration to finished work, retaining control of their artistic decisions and improving their craft.
gaps.currentMarkdown: Astrid provides a video editor, generation capabilities, agent-led timeline editing and creative packs. These are substantial foundations, but a coherent, demanding creator-led journey has **not been demonstrated by the evidence reviewed for this vision**.
gaps.missingMarkdown: The ceiling on sustained artistic control, continuity, revision and creative quality is not yet established through an ambitious end-to-end project.
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown: A real artist-led project is completed through repeated revision, with demonstrable continuity, editable results, preserved creative intent and serious creator/peer assessment. Record what the tools enabled, where they constrained ambition and what remains unresolved.

gaps.title: A culture that challenges people artistically
gaps.assessmentDetail: Open; founder-described community practices, no current program/outcome audit.
gaps.desiredMarkdown: People have compelling reasons to attempt work beyond their current abilities: artistic challenges, collaboration, critiques, showcases and high standards that encourage originality and growth.
gaps.currentMarkdown: The founder describes Banodoco community activity and art competitions. This is evidence of an intention and starting point, **not** evidence that a repeatable program demonstrably raises creative ambition or artistic quality.
gaps.missingMarkdown: Challenge formats, high-quality review, recognition and reliable feedback loops must become repeatable practices judged by their creative effects rather than participation metrics alone.
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown: Run a bounded challenge with clear artistic intent and fair participation; document artists' goals, feedback, completed work and whether it enabled more ambitious efforts. Incorporate genuine creator assessment, including negative findings and barriers.

gaps.title: A meaningful contributor-ownership model
gaps.assessmentDetail: Open; vision-level commitment, legal and operating terms not established.
gaps.desiredMarkdown: The people who meaningfully advance the collective have a genuine, understandable stake in the company behind it. The stated ambition is **100% ownership for contributors advancing the mission**, not merely participation rewards.
gaps.currentMarkdown: The ownership intention has been stated by the founder. No eligibility, allocation, vesting, governance, financing or legal instrument has been established within the materials reviewed for this vision.
gaps.missingMarkdown: A transparent and legally workable mechanism for translating meaningful contributions—creative, technical, mentoring or otherwise—into ownership and rights, including treatment of existing and future financing, has not yet been specified or implemented.
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown: An explicit owner decision and qualified legal/tax review of a concrete model covering eligible contributions, grants/allocations, governance, vesting, changes over time, financing and participant protections; then evidence of its authorized implementation. A declaration alone does not close this gap.

gaps.title: Agents learn from real creative work
gaps.desiredMarkdown: An agent routinely uses applicable earlier lessons **before** work, captures truthfully observed success or failure **during/after** work, learns within a user-owned private knowledge scope and can propose sanitized contributions to others with explicit permission.
gaps.currentMarkdown: Astrid Agent has executable creative tools and Runtime task/artifact records. Banodoco Hivemind has an evidence-bearing read/contribution system. The [source map](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/62bf308a959042b3f9119520315a46da65dcfc45/visions/references/compounding-intelligence/source-map.md) **does not establish a complete private/local → community → later-agent learning loop**.
gaps.missingMarkdown: Contextual retrieval, actual run-to-knowledge capture, safe private retention, consented contributions and proven benefits to a second agent session are not yet integrated end to end.
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown: Two real agent sessions: the first retrieves applicable knowledge and produces an observed, locally retained result; a subsequent session demonstrably uses that finding. Optional contribution retains provenance and only shares approved, sanitized information. Compare against raw search/no knowledge, including staleness and denial paths.

gaps.title: Independently owned, interoperable Hiveminds
gaps.desiredMarkdown: Independent personal, team and community knowledge datasets can preserve attribution, conditions, evidence and owner-controlled access while exchanging permitted references and learnings without merging into one central authority.
gaps.currentMarkdown: [Banodoco Hivemind](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/62bf308a959042b3f9119520315a46da65dcfc45/visions/references/compounding-intelligence/source-map.md) documents source-custodied messages, revisioned resources, an accepted search head and editorial contribution operations. The [uploaded October 29 protocol proposal](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/62bf308a959042b3f9119520315a46da65dcfc45/visions/references/compounding-intelligence/hivemind-protocol-proposal.md) proposes dataset-scoped entries, typed links and `find`/`inspect`/`contribute`. **These are not yet identical proven contracts.**
gaps.missingMarkdown: Versioned interoperable record/identity/reference and permission semantics, a local/private dataset implementation and one real cross-dataset boundary need a reconciled specification and evidence.
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown: Two separately owned datasets can exchange a scoped, independently attributed reference or approved sanitized result, preserving revision identity, provenance and access decisions; denied, stale and revoked cases do not leak source content. Banodoco behavior is preserved or safely, explicitly migrated with evidence.

gaps.title: Reliability across supported environments
gaps.assessmentDetail: Partially evidenced (2026-11-06; source is existing plan/queue evidence, not a new qualification).
gaps.desiredMarkdown: On each **declared supported** OS, device and deployment mode, people can reliably install, start, use, stop, update, roll back, repair and remove Astrid without losing work or being stranded by unexplained state. Support claims are backed by a maintained matrix of real-path evidence.
gaps.currentMarkdown: [Plan 08](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/62bf308a959042b3f9119520315a46da65dcfc45/plans/08-release1-install-update/plan.md) records a completed five-row hosted R1 installation/update gate, proving that *specific* paths worked on *specific* candidates. The [project queue](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/62bf308a959042b3f9119520315a46da65dcfc45/README.md) records Plan 07 as active with indicative Pinokio evidence and existing CI failures, while Plans 09/10 target broader routes and native qualification. This is **not** proof that all devices, browser variants or real engines are covered.
gaps.missingMarkdown: Real supported-environment coverage, failure/recovery paths, launcher and engine lifecycle, update/rollback qualification and current source/version coherence need broader and ongoing verification.
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown: A declared OS/browser/device/deployment matrix, including realistic new-install and update journeys, managed task/engine start and safe stop, recovery after interrupted operation, rollback/uninstall, preservation of project data, and meaningful negative controls. Exact candidate/source and platform evidence are attached. Unsupported cells remain explicit; do not claim "all devices" without defining the matrix.

gaps.title: Trustworthy user control and operation
gaps.desiredMarkdown: Human and agent actions are transparent, permissioned and recoverable. Creative state is not silently overwritten, external effects and resource use follow declared consent, untrusted execution has explicit safety boundaries, and stopping work does not destroy project data.
gaps.currentMarkdown: Astrid Runtime has versioned project/task authority and the App/Agent have meaningful editing and conflict primitives. [Plan 01](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/62bf308a959042b3f9119520315a46da65dcfc45/plans/01-installer-consent/plan.md) is for installer choice; [Plan 04](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/62bf308a959042b3f9119520315a46da65dcfc45/plans/04-concurrent-edits/plan.md) addresses concurrent edits; [Plan 15](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/62bf308a959042b3f9119520315a46da65dcfc45/plans/15-openshell-safe-execution/plan.md) proposes qualified sandbox boundaries. These are different safeguards; together they **have not yet established this general outcome**.
gaps.missingMarkdown: Unifying the user-facing expectations of consent, recoverability, isolation, safe resource use and simultaneous editing requires real integrated evidence, especially around agent actions and failure/refusal cases.
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown: Focused real-path tests of affirmative/denied consent, scoped permissions, concurrent user/agent writes and conflicts, preservation of unsaved work, safe cancellation/cleanup and honest sandbox limits. No claim of unrestricted security or isolation beyond verified environments.

gaps.title: Dependable end-to-end creative execution
gaps.desiredMarkdown: From a declared supported starting environment, a person and their agent can choose a suitable creative capability, connect or install what is needed with clear consent, execute real inference or processing, and receive a correct, editable result in the intended workspace—with understandable failures, cleanup and recovery.
gaps.currentMarkdown: Astrid has Runtime execution/task primitives, packs, generation integrations and the video editor. [Plan 02](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/62bf308a959042b3f9119520315a46da65dcfc45/plans/02-consistent-generation/plan.md) aims to establish consistent defaults and pinned stack on fixtures and a fresh Linux CPU setup, **explicitly not real inference**. [Plan 12](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/62bf308a959042b3f9119520315a46da65dcfc45/plans/12-multiple-inference-routes/plan.md) targets real multiple inference routes. [Plan 20](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/62bf308a959042b3f9119520315a46da65dcfc45/plans/20-zero-to-first-image/plan.md) targets a real first generated image on a timeline; [Plan 16](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/62bf308a959042b3f9119520315a46da65dcfc45/plans/16-streamlined-agent-experience/plan.md) improves agent readiness.
gaps.missingMarkdown: Reliably going from intent through correct model/provider readiness and task execution to usable creative output has not yet been demonstrated across chosen supported routes and recovery cases.
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown: A bounded, explicitly scoped real model execution on an approved environment, with setup/defaults, input/output identity, resource lifecycle, failure/retry/stop and a verified creative result in Astrid. Extend route/platform support only as qualified; realistic user effort and recoverability are measured.

gaps.title: Dependable pack and extension lifecycle
gaps.desiredMarkdown: Artists and agents can discover, install, enable, use, update, disable and safely roll back supported creative packs and their frontend/backend contributions. Compatibility, source identity, trust, ownership and project reference continuity remain understandable and reliable.
gaps.currentMarkdown: Agent has manifest-defined packs with actions, skills, UI and rendering contributions. App has trusted bundled extension lifecycle and editor SDK mechanisms. [Plan 06](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/62bf308a959042b3f9119520315a46da65dcfc45/plans/06-packs/plan.md) explicitly targets pack extraction and reliable installation, trust, transaction, rendering and editor integration. [Plan 11](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/62bf308a959042b3f9119520315a46da65dcfc45/plans/11-threejs-pack/plan.md) is a case of converting a first-party feature into a pack, but is not a generic workspace engine.
gaps.missingMarkdown: The practical lifecycle of reusable packs across Agent, Runtime and App still needs integrated, version-pinned proof of installation, runtime availability, use, safe upgrade/rollback, and handling of missing/broken contributions.
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown: Install a supported pack, discover its declared actions/UI, use it on project data, update and roll back safely with exact pinned source identity; show missing dependencies, rejected/untrusted cases, recovery and no loss of project references. Do not claim arbitrary dynamically generated third-party code can run safely without independent isolation evidence.

gaps.title: Portable creative components
gaps.desiredMarkdown: Real creative components (timeline, player, inspector, gallery and others) can move, dock, resize, float and nest within a declarative workspace without losing their state, supported behavior or resource bindings.
gaps.currentMarkdown: The [App source map](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/62bf308a959042b3f9119520315a46da65dcfc45/visions/references/liquid-software/source-map.md) identifies actual reusable editor views and a custom two-pane assembly. The standard editor shell still includes host-specific layout, gesture and context responsibilities. **This does not establish a general-purpose portable workspace host.**
gaps.missingMarkdown: Component definitions, instances, presentation/lifecycle and positioning are not yet proven independently composable across workspace layouts and domains.
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown: Rearrange the **real** player, inspector and timeline; retain playback, editing, selection and recovery state; save/restore the layout. Then host a genuinely different domain component using the same contract, without modifying the main editor shell.

gaps.title: Agent-accessible workspace composition
gaps.desiredMarkdown: An agent and a person use the same supported workspace operations to open, place, attach, bind, focus and restore component instances. Changes are inspectable, scoped, reversible and compatible with live creative work.
gaps.currentMarkdown: Astrid Agent has pack/skill/action discovery. Astrid App has extensions, commands and scoped editing contexts. The [source review](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/62bf308a959042b3f9119520315a46da65dcfc45/visions/references/liquid-software/source-map.md) has **not** established a public, domain-neutral workspace manipulation API.
gaps.missingMarkdown: Spatial **placement/attachment** and functional **resource binding** need explicit, validated operations; proximity alone must not silently connect data. Agents should compose existing software without generating frontend code for ordinary layout changes.
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown: An agent arranges the same real components as a user, binds the correct timeline/selection/clock, offers reversible operations, does not clobber user edits, and restores a prior workspace from a saved representation.

gaps.title: Composable frontend and backend contributions
gaps.desiredMarkdown: A creator or agent can discover and use one pack's creative capability, its typed results and its appropriate frontend components together—extending opinionated tools without bespoke, duplicate integrations.
gaps.currentMarkdown: Astrid Agent pack manifests can declare actions, UI, renderers and skills. Astrid App has a video-editor extension SDK, typed data lanes, proposals and rendering hooks. Current pack UI hosting is still tied to supported host entries; **general component-owned extension points and unified live composition are unproven**.
gaps.missingMarkdown: Common identity and discovery across pack contributions, semantic resource/result bindings, component-defined extension hosts and safe activation need proving beyond the default video editor.
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown: An installed/trusted music capability yields a typed beat-grid result used in a real timeline view and music control surface. The interface can be rearranged, results correctly track source-to-timeline coordinates, and updates follow existing authoritative domain editing/undo. A second distinct extension domain validates generality.

projects.title: Pinokio basic (R1.1)
projects.goalMarkdown: Prove users can install, start, stop (including while busy), update and remove Astrid through Pinokio on Linux, macOS and Windows, with a separate three-row hosted gate. Shipped on indicative evidence (5 Nov); gaps in the plan.

projects.title: Zero-to-first-image onboarding
projects.goalMarkdown: Go from an existing inference setup to a generated image visible on the timeline through one simple command, with tested recovery and minimal agent effort.

projects.title: Install and update confidence
projects.goalMarkdown: Make installing and updating dependable on all three OSes: one update path, and a real hosted test for every install, update, rollback and removal route.

projects.title: Installer consent
projects.goalMarkdown: Let users choose what Astrid installs and enables, with clear consent, saved preferences, and predictable behavior.

projects.title: Consistent generation path
projects.goalMarkdown: Make supported generation choose consistent defaults and set up a compatible, pinned stack, proven on fixtures and a fresh Linux install; real model inference is not proven here.
projects.estimate: 4–5 days after Plan 01 (includes the RunPod dry-run work, the installed-package test and the final rebase), plus a Linux x86_64 environment
projects.waitingOn: Plan 01 (from phase 3); a Linux x86_64 environment for task V2 only

projects.title: Pinokio qualification
projects.goalMarkdown: Engine Stop/Quit refusal veto, direct custody and fully-local mode, qualified natively.

projects.title: Refined concurrent editing
projects.goalMarkdown: Keep users in control: agent edits must respect user edits, surface conflicts, and retry safely without silently overwriting changes.

projects.title: Release fixes integration
projects.goalMarkdown: Bring the accepted fixes together into a coherent release while preserving existing behavior.

projects.title: Packs v1.3
projects.goalMarkdown: Simplify and standardize how packs work, moving pack-specific features out of core while preserving supported workflows.
projects.waitingOn: owner's go; a Playwright browser for the App checks

projects.title: Three.js as a pack
projects.goalMarkdown: Move the existing built-in Three.js functionality into a native pack that remains included by default, with current behavior preserved through conversion.

projects.title: Multiple inference routes (Wan2GP)
projects.goalMarkdown: Keep VibeComfy as the primary route and add Wan2GP through the shared generation path, with shared setup, task/resource ownership, model lifecycle, and cleanup.

projects.title: Execution host refactor
projects.goalMarkdown: Split the oversized execution host into clear, maintainable modules while preserving supported execution behavior.

projects.title: Repository cleanup
projects.goalMarkdown: Make the repositories easy to navigate and maintain by removing proven clutter and consolidating code, docs, and tooling.

projects.title: Sandboxed execution with OpenShell
projects.goalMarkdown: Let users onboard into an isolated full Astrid stack, including the app/frontend and backend, with explicit permissions and tested boundaries.

projects.title: Streamlined agent setup and execution
projects.goalMarkdown: Simplify account connection and execution, and let contributors add an agent in one place while preserving alternative agents and pack runs.

projects.title: VibeComfy extensibility with H3_AV
projects.goalMarkdown: Make it easy to build and share higher-level tools on VibeComfy workflows, using H3_AV to prove reusable extension primitives.

projects.title: Extensible timeline editing
projects.goalMarkdown: Provide reliable timeline editing primitives as a pack that people and agents can extend with their own views, tools, and creative workflows.

projects.title: First-principles documentation
projects.goalMarkdown: Make Astrid understandable to humans and agents through a clear path from its purpose and central skill to workflows, pack design, and precise references.

projects.title: Astrid website
projects.goalMarkdown: Build the scroll journey below the Astrid homepage hero: three sections and a vision finale that re-explain the hero's notes, with the sky following the visitor's time of day. The rest of the website is not yet scoped.

projects.title: Hivemind protocol
projects.goalMarkdown: Reconcile the Hivemind protocol proposal with real knowledge records, then prove independent private/community datasets can exchange permitted evidence.

projects.title: Continuous agent learning
projects.goalMarkdown: Make retrieval, observed local learning and optional contributions a real Astrid Agent workflow.

projects.title: Agent-powered liquid workspace
projects.goalMarkdown: Prove real components can be positioned, bound and adapted by people and agents without losing editing state.

projects.title: Release 1: install and update
projects.goalMarkdown: Ship R1: new users install and update on Linux, macOS and Windows; R0 users on Linux and macOS upgrade without data loss, proven by the five-row hosted gate.
